findings.title: A claim held through S_WATCH is refused on a stale r_busy when WATCH ends; if the far caller left meanwhile, the refusal re-busies a released trunk with CLAIM for good and the neighbour takes it as a new seizure
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:282 exempts S_WATCH from att_refuse (comment 275-281: 'a claim waits that out'), so the unit's att stays up (net_unit.v:673-674, CL_ACK waits only for att_ack). WATCH ends with r_release and a move to S_IDLE (mini_marker.v:550-552) or S_DRAIN (542-548). pulse_reg clears busy one edge after release_it (pulse_reg.v:117-118), so on the first tick in S_IDLE/S_DRAIN r_busy is still 1. att_refuse (282) then fires, and att_take (273-274) never gets the tick the register is actually free. The marker writes trunk <- 03 with BSY and CLM (320-327). The design intent (the WATCH comment; newimpl/README.md 'A claim ... waits rather than being refused') is a take. If the far caller hung up during the wait, the trunk has already released itself on its fM fall (port.v:176-194). The refusal then latches 03/BSY/CLM on a port whose M is down and whose source (03) never rises: there is no edge, so it is BUSY for good. CLM drives backward A = 1 for good (port.v:153). The neighbour's port is free, so it shows M up with BUSY down and st clear, and its classifier holds it as an incoming seizure (net_unit.v:609-621): a HOLD, a monitor cell and a forward. The monitor never releases because M never breaks (its only release is d_clr, 256 ms of break).
findings.trigger: tb_attw: A=2 2, B=2 3, A11-B11 and A12-B12 (tb_net's plant, scale 8). B20 dials 2 1 and is connected; B's marker enters S_WATCH and B20's line chatters (1 ms break / 2 ms make, so it is never settled and never gone). A20 dials 1 2 3; B's monitor claims B11 and att waits. scen 1: A20 stays on and the chatter stops 20 ms later. scen 2: A20 hangs up the moment att rises and the chatter goes on 150 ms, past B11's own release.
findings.consequence: scen 1: a network call the design says should be served gets cannot-complete; A20 hears 03 and B22 never rings. scen 2: B11 stays BUSY with CLAIM listening to 03, and A11 is held by A as a phantom incoming seizure with a monitor cell (1 of 2) held for good, 800 ms after every phone is on-hook. A tried to forward the phantom (n_nofwd 1). At a transit the phantom would be forwarded, holding a trunk per link, a monitor per exchange and a resolver per hub for good (reasoned; A had no onward direction).

findings.fix: Minimum and safe: delete '(state != S_WATCH)' from att_refuse (mini_marker.v:282), so every claim is answered at once while its trunk is still up (tested, +fixwatch). This costs the claims that arrive in a WATCH, which the RTL already refuses today, only later. To keep the take the comment intends, add '&& !r_release' (one gate; tested, +fixatt), but only together with a bound on the wait (see queued-claim-late-attach-wrong-number); on its own it moves the late-attach hazard onto the first claim. Also make the unit's refusal path safe on a dead trunk: gate w_claim and the refusal on the trunk's M still being up (the claiming cell's probe mp_m), a gate or two.
findings.realistic: At real timers every local connect opens a WATCH of the words plus SETTLE (2 x T_ARM = 32 ms). A claim arriving in it is refused, about the local-connect rate x 33 ms of claims (~0.1% at a busy exchange), and gracefully. WATCH stretches to CLR (256 ms) when the local caller abandons inside SETTLE, and to NODIG (10 s) on a chattering line (mini_marker.v:538-539 anticipates chatter). The permanent stuck state needs the wait to outlast the far trunk's own release (far caller gone + T_REL 256 ms): the chattering-line WATCH, or a local and a far abandon within ~30 ms of each other. Rare, but permanent, and it spreads to the neighbour.

findings.title: A second claim queued behind one held in S_WATCH is attached late, in the middle of the far caller's h: wrong number
findings.mechanism: One claim handler: w_claim needs cl_st == CL_IDLE (net_unit.v:487), so while att 1 waits (CL_ACK, 674) a second monitor that has heard its own e b keeps m_want (641) with its CLAIM unwritten, and its cell stops counting (M_DONE, 'two digits and no more'). When the CLAIM finally goes, the cell is freed (666-668). Nothing watches that trunk between the monitor's b and the register's attach. When WATCH ends, att 1 is refused (previous finding), cl_st returns to idle, claim 2's CLAIM goes out and att 2 rises. The register is now free, so the marker takes it (mini_marker.v:273-274, 305-319) at whatever point the far caller has reached. pulse_rx counts only from the attach (pulse_rx.v:244-249; pulse_reg.v:106-107), so the pulses of h before it are lost and h is counted short. Nothing bounds the wait or checks for breaks during it.

findings.consequence: A21 dialled 1 2 3 3 2 (B32). B's register attached to B12 13 ms into h, counted 2 pulses, and B22 rang: a wrong number the caller cannot see. A queued claim also holds a monitor cell (NMON = 2) for the whole wait, so a further seizure arriving then may go unwatched.

findings.fix: Never let att wait an unbounded time. Simplest: answer claims at once in WATCH (drop the S_WATCH exemption, tested +fixwatch); then only S_READ with a free register delays att, by at most a pass plus 8 frames. If a wait is kept for capacity, bound it with a tick_1k count in CL_ACK (refuse after ~ID). Keep the claiming monitor cell on the trunk until att_ack, and turn the answer into a refusal if its brk_stb fires meanwhile: one cell held a few ticks longer, a flag and a ribbon bit or a unit-side refusal. Cost: a few gates.
findings.realistic: The wait must reach into h. With a compliant telephone (720 ms minimum between digits, network.md 4) h begins about 590 ms or more after the claim-want. A CLR-length WATCH (<= ~290 ms) ends before that, and the late attach then catches all of h s (delayed, but correct). Only a chattering-line WATCH (up to NODIG 10 s) or a fast, non-compliant dialler reaches it. Rare, and a wrong number when it happens.

findings.title: F_WRITE ignores f_cancel: an UNHOLD pushed on the sweep's last tick is followed by the forward's leg and way back, and the dead seizure's port, its leg and a resolver are held for good
findings.mechanism: C_UNHOLD pushes the unhold and sets f_cancel (net_unit.v:590-594, 593). F_WANT (714) and F_HUNT (720-724) honour f_cancel; F_WRITE (725-743) does not. F_HUNT reads the old f_cancel on the tick the UNHOLD sets it. The sweep's last read is port 70 (h_idx = 1 + 9 x 63 mod 64, 769-770), whose word ends in port 00's bit-time, so CONFIRM counts ports 00..77 and h_done is always raised at port 77's visit (779-785). A seizure on 77 whose first low sample is that visit therefore gets C_UNHOLD and h_done on one tick. The UNHOLD (77 <- 00, b 0) is pushed, F_HUNT goes to F_WRITE, and the next tick pushes the leg (13 <- 77, B) and, because there is one leg, the way back (77 <- 13, B) (732-736). The order on cable B is unhold, leg, way back. At the real T_ARM the ~12 ms seizure never armed 77's fM; 77 listens to a leg whose M is 0 and the leg listens to dead 77, so no detector will ever fall (port.v:176-194). The resolver (rs_two) waits for R_LEG or R_GONE (688-689), and 77's BUSY never drops.
findings.trigger: tb_fcan: one exchange, trunks looped to themselves, 77 facing W (blip on its incoming A) and 13 facing E. T_ARM 16 ms (real), other timers scale 8. The seizure on 77 ends at scan 16 during CONFIRM (it stood 12.25 ms).
findings.consequence: 77 and 13 stay BUSY and a resolver (1 of 2) stays held 400 ms after the seizure died and for good. A second occurrence exhausts NRES = 2 and the exchange stops forwarding. The trunk group loses two channels.
findings.evidence: /home/joel/telco/newimpl/build/flood/work/audit/cableb/run_fcan_mode0.log: '[66 ms] seizure on 77 ends: it stood 12250 us, fM armed 0' / '[67 ms] sweep done (h_done) ... last CONFIRM visit port 77' / '[67 ms] UNHOLD pushed for 77; fst 2' / '[67 ms] FORWARD pushed: f_in 77 f_ok 0100 f_cancel 1' / cable B in order: 'dst 77 src 00 bsy 0', 'dst 13 src 77 bsy 1', 'dst 77 src 13 bsy 1' / '[485 ms] 77 addr 13 bsy 1 BUSY 1; 13 addr 77 bsy 1 BUSY 1; res 01'. findings.fix: In F_WRITE, 'if (f_cancel) fst <= F_IDLE' ahead of w_fwd, and gate w_fwd with !f_cancel (tested, +fixfc; one gate). Alternatively F_HUNT takes the cancel combinationally from (w_cls && cst == C_UNHOLD && cls_port == f_in).
findings.realistic: It needs a seizure that dies in the millisecond before the forwarder's sweep ends, about 11-13 ms after it arrived (a far origin's guard abandoning, glare, a blip), on the trunk in socket 77. Other ports are exposed only if the UNHOLD lands in the 1-3 ticks while w_fwd waits behind a claim, hold or origin write. The permanent state needs a one-leg forward (a chain); with 2-3 legs, R_GONE sees 77 free and drops them. Rare but permanent. The benches' scale-8 T_ARM of 2 ms hides it, because the port arms within the sweep and releases itself.

findings.title: The C_HOLD watch writes the hold away on a dial break, the make is taken as a fresh seizure, and a second monitor attached after pulse 1 of e claims a wrong code
findings.mechanism: C_HOLD (net_unit.v:584-588) goes to C_UNHOLD on any sample of M low within T_ARM+2 ms of the hold, a dial break as much as a death, and writes the port free (590-594). The M-low visit clears st[port] (566-567). After the unhold bsy is 0, and at the make M is up with BUSY down (port.v:147: fm && !m holds BUSY only during the break), so cls_seen (283-284) re-classifies it. The result is a second HOLD and a second monitor cell (612-615) attached after pulse 1 of e. The first cell counts e correctly; the second counts e-1 and claims if (e-1, b) is this exchange's code. The known T_ARM hold-watch fix therefore turns a live seizure's break into a new rise, which breaks the monitor rule 'counts only a seizure whose rise it saw'.

findings.consequence: A caller dialling 1 3 4 2 1 (code 3 4, nobody) is claimed by C and C21 rings. Wrong number in 3 of the 4 offsets inside C's watch; the offset past the watch and the +60 ms control are clean.

findings.fix: Treat M low in C_HOLD as a death only if it outlasts a dial break. Go to a C_LOW state and write nothing; M high again means C_IDLE (the port arms during the make, which stands >= T_ARM; BUSY stays set, so st is set again and the make is not re-classified); M low for >= ID means UNHOLD. Cost: one state and a compare on cls_ms. In that rare case the classifier is held up to ~128 ms.
findings.realistic: At real timers the exposed exchange is the one whose seizure arrived 2-20 ms before the caller's first break (hold at +2..3 ms, watch to T_ARM+2 = 18 ms after it). The guard puts the first break at >= 128 ms after the origin's seizure, so at the RTL's ~13 ms a hop that is hop ~10, just beyond network.md 3.2's 8-hop rule. It moves nearer when hops slow under load: +10 ms waiting for a sweep in progress, and the classifier taking one seizure per ~18 ms. In effect the guard's reach shrinks by 18 ms (14% of the 128 ms tap). With a compliant dial the first break comes ~590 ms after the seizure, so only a fast dialler near the guard is exposed. It is reproduced at scale 8 because there the sweep is 8x longer relative to the guard.

findings.title: The unit's WAIT is a hand constant with a 93-tick margin, not derived from the serialiser, and mini-marker.md still gives the old figure
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:104 has WAIT = 640. The marker's longest transaction, from the edge it samples go (/UREQ) to its '244 releasing, is 547 ticks (ctl_queue.v:169-181, ctl_write.v:253-297: one tick to load, 16 x 32 shift, 32 strobe, 2 to hand back), so the margin is 93 ticks (23 us). exchange/mini-marker.md:313 still says 1152 ticks 'a word read'. WAIT is not tied to ctl_write's DIV or to the word length; ctl_write.v's jumper note about SCLK free-running off HCLK/4, or a 17th bit, would change the word time and silently remove the margin, and then b_clash.
findings.trigger: Any change to DIV or CWW without a matching edit to WAIT.
findings.consequence: Two '244s on cable B, a corrupted write and a runt WR; today none (b_clash 0 in every baseline and every audit run).
findings.evidence: Arithmetic above. tb_net 17 exercises the same-edge case and stays clash-free (work/base-net.log PASS).
findings.fix: localparam WAIT = (`CWW + 1) * DIV + margin, shared from exch.vh; update mini-marker.md:313. No hardware cost.

findings.title: w_claim maps every matching resolver's legs onto the same five slots; two would overwrite each other silently
findings.mechanism: w_claim pushes the CLAIM on slot 0 and each rs_mine resolver's legs on slots j2+1 (net_unit.v:659-663), and cnt_claim reserves room for all of them (474). If two resolvers share rs_in, the later loop iteration overwrites the earlier one's slots. Leg drops are then lost without ovf, and those legs stay up, listening to the claimed trunk, until the call ends.
findings.trigger: Two resolvers holding forwards of one port: a stale resolver whose R_GONE has not been acted on when the port is re-seized, forwarded and claimed. That needs w_res starved for seconds, which the one-pusher-a-tick scheme never does.
findings.consequence: Downstream trunks held for the length of the call; no wrong number.
findings.evidence: Reasoning only; not reachable in any realistic sequence found.
findings.fix: Act on one rs_mine resolver per claim tick, or assert popc(rs_mine) <= 1 in the benches. A gate.

sound.claim: No two pushers write push_v in one tick, and no push is lost to a later non-blocking assignment
sound.why: w_claim, w_cls, w_orig, w_fwd, w_res and w_ev are mutually exclusive by construction (net_unit.v:487-497). Each pusher's slot map fits in 5: the claim uses slot 0 plus legs 1..4; origin, forwarder and resolver use slots 0..3 plus slot 4 for the way back. The later push_v[k] assignments inside one pusher's block are to distinct bits. The only exception is the latent two-resolver case reported separately.

sound.claim: The unit's queue can never overflow and a pusher that must write (UNHOLD, drops) never waits for ever
sound.why: room counts this tick's arrivals (ctl_queue.v:129). Only one pusher decides a tick, and its words land the next tick, when free space is >= the room it checked, so ovf cannot light. The queue drains at 1 word per 547 ticks once granted, and the grant depends only on the unit's own /UREQ (net_unit.v:225-232). The marker can delay the grant by at most one word. Pushers are event-driven with no self-sustaining loop, so room always returns. A lower pusher that needs less room may go ahead of a higher one waiting for more, and the higher one gets room within a few words.

sound.claim: Event words cannot write a port and cannot delay a call
sound.why: G = 0 is gated into WR at every block (block.v:113). ctl_queue drops an event when fewer than 6 entries are free (ctl_queue.v:107), without ovf. w_ev is the lowest pusher. Merging two events of one kind needs two origin hunts or glares inside the few ticks w_ev can be deferred, which cannot happen.

sound.claim: Cable B has no clash between the two masters
sound.why: The marker starts only with /UREQ high (go = ureq_n); a word it starts on the very edge /UREQ falls ends its '244 547 ticks later, and the unit drives at 641, a 93-tick margin. Unit to marker: the unit's oe falls on the edge q_empty rises and the marker starts one tick (244 ns) later. A unit that re-requests after emptying waits WAIT again, because granted clears. b_clash was 0 in all five baselines and in every audit run (tb_net 17 provokes the same-edge case).

sound.claim: The marker is not starved by the unit, and the unit is never starved by the marker
sound.why: /UREQ is low only while the unit's queue is non-empty. The worst burst is 16 words: 640 + 16 x 547 ticks = 2.3 ms, typically one pusher's <= 5 words in 0.8 ms. While it waits the marker's words sit in its 8-deep queue: dial tone off, a connect or a refusal comes up to ~2 ms late. S_WATCH holds its no-digit timer while its words are queued (mini_marker.v:541), and nothing times out. The marker never has more than one word in flight when the unit wants the bus.

sound.claim: CLAIM reaches the port before the marker's refusal, and the refusal lands after it
sound.why: att rises only when the unit's queue is empty, all words out including the CLAIM (net_unit.v:673, q_empty includes t == IDLE). The marker's refusal is pushed only after att. att_take writes nothing, and every later marker write to that trunk carries CLM (ctx_clm). tb_net 8 confirms.

sound.claim: FIFO order is enough for every same-port pair inside the unit
sound.why: Seize then drop (N_SEIZE, then N_DROP or dmo), hold then unhold, CLAIM then leg drops (slot 0 first), and leg then way back (slot 4 last) all go through the one queue in decision order. The one bad pair (UNHOLD before a forward that should have been cancelled) is a decision defect in F_WRITE, not an ordering one.

sound.claim: The marker's and the unit's words to the same port do not interleave harmfully
sound.why: The marker writes a trunk port only as a claimed caller, after the CLAIM. The unit writes a line port only at N_DONE (caller <- trunk). The one overlap is N_DONE against the marker's r_gone write to the same caller (net_unit.v:818-822 does not re-check o_gone). The unit's word normally lands first and the marker's frees the caller. In the reverse order, needing the marker already mid-word inside a 1-tick window, the caller port stays BUSY on the trunk only until the trunk's backward A falls (fE), which is transient.

sound.claim: A word landing mid-turn never shows a half-written state
sound.why: The '273 takes addr, bsy and clm on one WR edge (port.v:193-194), and M and BUSY are sampled at one instant (probe.v a_stb), so a reader sees before or after, never a mix. A write between the sweep's select and its use is caught by the CONFIRM pass. Between the unit's own decision and its word landing, `mine` keeps the classifier off the port.

sound.claim: The flood_go / YIELD / done-nogo-local handshake cannot desynchronise
sound.why: flood_go is ignored unless the origin bank is N_IDLE, and the bank returns there within ms of done, nogo or local, while the next key 1 is at least ID (128 ms) away. o_gone cannot be missed inside N_HUNT, because the register cannot be released and re-attached within a sweep (r_gone needs 256 ms of break after the key's 128 ms make).

sound.claim: f_cancel works where it is read
sound.why: F_WANT (714) and F_HUNT at h_done (720-724) honour it. The control run run_fcan_mode1.log (a death a pass before the sweep's end) cancels cleanly. Only F_WRITE is exposed (reported).

sound.claim: Cable B capacity is not a bottleneck
sound.why: A word is 17 bit-times at 128 kHz, 133 us; the unit's first word after idle costs 290 us with WAIT, so about 7,500 words/s. A flood costs each exchange HOLD + L legs (+1 way back) + L-1 drops + 1 way back, about 2L+2 <= 8 words; an origin 2k+2; a local call 4 marker words. At 1 flood/s network-wide, a busy network, cable B is ~0.2% occupied. The limits are the single origin bank and forwarder, the one register, the classifier (one seizure per ~18 ms) and the 10 ms sweep, all 2-3 orders of magnitude tighter.

sound.claim: Release-beats-write on the same tick (port.v:193) is benign
sound.why: A WR edge coinciding with a detector fall on the same port loses the write. The window is one 244 ns tick in a millisecond, and in every case found the release is the right outcome.

notes:
I found seven defects on cable B, the unit's writes and the claim handshake: two wrong numbers, two permanent stuck states and three minor. Four are reproduced on the snapshot RTL; the queue and the bus themselves are sound.

**How the benches were run**
- The four directed benches and their logs are in /home/joel/telco/newimpl/build/flood/work/audit/cableb/.
- tb_brk ran on the plain snapshot (work/RTL.list).
- tb_attw, tb_att2 and tb_fcan ran on copies of mini_marker.v and net_unit.v (mini_marker_k.v, net_unit_k.v, RTL_k.list) that differ from the snapshot only by three plusarg knobs, all off by default: +fixatt, +fixwatch and +fixfc.
- With the knobs off the copies behave as the snapshot: run_attw_scen1_rebuilt_knobsoff.log is identical to run_attw_scen1.log, and the patch is 3 lines per file (diff shown in the session).
- The five baselines are green, and b_clash / ovf were 0 in every run.

**Findings, in order of consequence**
1. **Wrong number from a queued second claim.** It is attached late, mid-digit, after the first claim was held through S_WATCH (tb_att2: 1 2 3 3 2 rang B22).
2. **Late refusal re-busies a released trunk.** A claim held through S_WATCH is refused on a stale r_busy. If the far caller left during the wait, the refusal lands on a trunk that has already released: permanent BUSY+CLM, and the neighbour holds a phantom seizure with a monitor for good (tb_attw scen 2). This is also a spec mismatch: the code comment and the README say the claim waits and is taken.
3. **F_WRITE ignores f_cancel.** Port 77, its leg and a resolver are held for good at the real T_ARM (tb_fcan).
4. **The C_HOLD watch unholds on a dial break**, and a re-attached monitor mis-hears e (tb_brk). This is cross-slice, but it is the hold/unhold pair.

**Fixes to use**
- The safe att fix is +fixwatch: answer every claim at once, and never let att wait through S_WATCH.
- The one-gate +fixatt (skip the r_release tick) serves the claim as the comment intends. It fixes scenarios 1 and 2 but moves the late-attach hazard onto the first claim, so pair it with a bounded wait if you keep it.
- Also harden the claim itself: gate w_claim and the refusal on the trunk's M still being up.

**Real timers.** None of the four needs scale-8 slack to exist, but each needs a rare coincidence at real timers:
- The late-claim wrong number and the late refusal need a long S_WATCH (a chattering local line, or an abandon inside SETTLE) and a far caller hanging up or dialling at the wrong moment.
- tb_fcan ran at the real T_ARM, because scale 8 hides the stuck state there.
- The hold-watch wrong number is reproduced only at scale 8. At real timers it exposes the hop whose seizure arrives 2-20 ms before the first break: hop ~10 at the RTL's ~13 ms a hop, nearer under load. It shortens the guard's reach by about 18 ms.

**Architectural caveat.** The 16-deep, 5-wide queue is a model part (README says the unit's sequencer is not drawn). The ordering arguments here — one pusher a tick, FIFO, q_empty before att — would need re-checking against a word-at-a-time 74HC sequencer.

**Housekeeping.** Build dirs are deleted (the audit dir is 280 KB) and nothing was written outside the audit directory.

findings.title: A seizure written away inside T_ARM (C_UNHOLD) keeps its monitor cell. The cell then counts the next call on that trunk one digit out of step and claims it: a wrong number
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:611-615 gives the first free cell to a seizure at w_cls. 584-588 watches the hold for T_ARM, and when M falls, 590-594 writes the hold away and sets f_cancel, but never touches m_held/m_st/m_armed. A cell is freed only by a digit mismatch (635-639), a claim (666-668) or d_clr, which is CLR = 256 ms of break (647-649). The port is now free: BUSY is clear and st was cleared by the M-low sample at 566-567. A new seizure within CLR is therefore classified again (283-284, 570) and gets a SECOND cell (612): two cells watch one port. In the stale cell, pulse_rx (pulse_rx.v:84-90) counted the short seizure's death as a pulse (a break >= HIT). It then takes the re-seizure's make as the end of a digit (pulse_rx.v:96-99, ID), so it hears a digit 1 that nobody dialled, then the new call's e as its b. If the new call's first break comes before ID of the rise, the cell instead hears (1+e) as e and b as b. Either pair matching OWN_E/OWN_B goes M_DONE, then CLAIM (656-671), then att. The mini marker attaches its register (mini_marker.v:305-319), and the register reads the call's (b h) or (h s) as the local number.
findings.trigger: (1) An incoming trunk seizure that dies inside T_ARM (16 ms). Causes: the far origin's guard abandoning on a break inside 16 ms of its seizure (tb_net scenario 7's case); a far origin taking glare on one direction as its claim and dropping its other directions via dmo within a few ms; a far resolver doing the same on a glared leg. (2) The same channel seized again within CLR (256 ms). Causes: a far transit's forwarder re-using the lowest free channel for the next flood (~15 ms), or the far origin's next caller keying 1 at once. (3) A code match. Variant (1,e): any exchange whose e is 1 (by convention the backbone, 10-17) claims every such call whose e equals its b, at e's ID, before b is dialled. Variant (e+1,b): any exchange claims when the caller's first break falls inside ID of the re-seizure, which a fast caller the 128 ms guard still admits can do.
findings.consequence: The far caller is connected, both ways, to a line on the wrong exchange, and nothing anywhere notices. In the (1,e) variant the origin even accepts the claim before b is dialled (see origin-accepts-early-claim). The true destination, if it claims, loses the race or is dropped. Side effect: each short seizure also holds a cell for 256 ms (stale-cell-starves-monitors).
findings.evidence: work/audit/monclaim/run_mc_all.log, scenario 1, scale 8, exchange 13. [1193 ms] cell 0 given to the 0.9 ms blip on T11. [1194] busy1x->0: hold written away, cell still held. [1213] 'port=11/11': a second cell on T11. [1229] stale cell st=2: it took '1' as e. [1349] stale cell want -> CLAIM on T11 (bkA=...1), leg T16 dropped, att@11, reg=1 on 11. Register dig=0022; [1629-1630] connect. 'FAIL SAFETY: X (13) did not claim a call dialled to 3x' and 'FAIL ... no phone at X rings' (X22 rang). Real timers: run_real13_sc1.log shows the same 3 FAILs, ringing=...40000 (X22). The (e+1,b) variant is in run_mc42_sc5.log (scale 8) and run_real42_sc5.log (real timers): exchange 42 claims a call dialled 1 3 2 2 1 and X21 rings. End to end, two exchanges at real timers, work/audit/monclaim/run_mc2.log: A seizes A11 at 450 ms; X holds it and gives a cell at 453, writes the hold away at 456; A's guard drops A11 at 464. A21 gets the register at 467 and keys 1; A re-seizes A11 at 704 ms (240 ms later). X gives a second cell at 707; the stale cell goes st=2 at 835 ('1'). A21 dials 3 and X claims at 1894 ms; A shows claimed=1 at 1895 while in origin state 4 (N_NET, b not yet dialled). A21 dials 2 2 1, X connects X22 at 3894, and A21 hears X22's tx go 1 then 0. Both exchanges were idle afterwards.
findings.fix: (a) The classifier keeps the cell it gave (cls_cell, one flip-flop a cell) and frees that cell in the C_UNHOLD write. (b) A cell lets go on a break no dial makes: its own timer's ID tap (monitor.md 6: Q7, 128 ms) ANDed with M low, one gate a cell; this also closes rc-tolerance-reseize. Total cost is about one package. Both are implemented in work/audit/monclaim/rtl_fix/{net_unit.v,pulse_rx.v} (diff in work/audit/monclaim/fix.patch). With the fix, scenarios 1, 3 and 5 are safe at scale 8 and at real timers (run_fix13_all.log, run_fix42_sc5.log, run_realfix13_all.log, run_realfix42_sc5.log) and the end-to-end bench is safe (run_fix_mc2.log: no claim, X22 not rung, A21 does not follow X22). The control and burst scenarios are unchanged, and the tree's tb_net passes on the fixed RTL (run_fix_tbnet.log: 88 checks, 0 errors). Defence in depth: origin-accepts-early-claim.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: reproduced end to end at the board's timers. It is rare. It needs a short seizure (a guard abandon inside T_ARM, or glare taken as a claim by an origin or resolver), then that channel re-seized within 256 ms, then a code match: 1 in 8 re-seized floods for an e=1 exchange, about 1 in 64 otherwise. The origin route in tb_mc2 needed A21 to key within about 45 ms of dial tone (6 ms of margin to CLR), which is unlikely by hand but easy for a data card pulsing DTR. The transit-forwarder route is the likely one under load, because the sweep re-picks the lowest free channel. At scale 8 the origin route cannot happen: one key costs 12 + 16 ms plus an unscaled ~11 ms sweep, more than CLR = 32 ms. That is why no tree bench met it.

findings.title: Every seizure shorter than T_ARM holds a monitor cell for 256 ms. With NMON = 2, two of them make the exchange deaf to its own calls
findings.mechanism: Same root as stale-cell-after-unhold: C_UNHOLD (net_unit.v:590-594) writes the hold away at once, but the cell given at 612-615 stays until CLR (647-649). A seizure classified meanwhile finds m_free1 empty and gets no cell, so it is 'unwatched here, for good' (monitor.md 4).
findings.trigger: Two short seizures (glare or guard abandons on two links), then within 256 ms a flood that dials this exchange.
findings.consequence: No claim. The origin waits T_CLAIM (2 s after b) and gives cannot-complete, holding a trunk on every link and its only register throughout.
findings.evidence: run_mc_all.log and run_real13_all.log, scenario 3: 'ok OBSERVE: both cells held by the blips', 'ok T15 held', 'FAIL LIVENESS: X claims a call dialled to it (1 3) on T15', 'FAIL X25 rings'. Passes with the fix (run_fix13_all.log, run_realfix13_all.log).
findings.fix: Fix (a) of stale-cell-after-unhold.
findings.realistic: Real timing (reproduced at real timers). Any short seizure costs a cell for a quarter second; in bursts of glare it adds to monitor-pool blocking.

findings.title: The T_ARM hold watch (C_HOLD) serialises the classifier. Each seizure's cell and forward start about 19 ms later per seizure ahead of it, and monitor rule 1 (a cell only for a rise seen within a scan) is not implemented
findings.mechanism: cls_seen needs cst == C_IDLE (net_unit.v:283), and C_HOLD lasts until cls_ms > T_ARM+1 (584-588), 18 ticks at real timers. A seizure that rises meanwhile keeps st clear and is taken at a later pass; its cell (612-615) and forward (616-621) start then, however old it is. The comment at 604-608 assumes 'a millisecond or two after the rise'. monitor.md 3 rule 1 and 4 require a cell within one scan of the rise or none at all. pulse_rx's arm semantics (pulse_rx.v:72-90): a break already in progress at arm is counted only if >= HIT of it remains, and an earlier break is lost. So a late cell counts e short.
findings.trigger: k trunk seizures reaching one exchange within about 20 ms: floods from several neighbours, a flood arriving on more than one link, or a hub.
findings.consequence: Measured rise-to-hold for five simultaneous seizures: 2, 21, 40, 59, 78 ms at real timers (2, 7, 12, 17, 23 at scale 8). Rise to the onward leg carrying M: 14 ms for the first seizure and 33 ms for the second, against the 12 ms a hop the 128 ms guard is sized on (monitor.md 3.5, network.md 3.2). That eats the guard's hop budget. A cell for the k-th seizure arms about 19(k-1) ms late. With NMON >= 3-5 (monitor.md 4's sizing for larger networks), or at a deep hop where the guard's slack is small, the cell or the downstream exchange misses the first pulse of e: a partial count, and a false claim wherever the short code matches. With NMON = 2 at hop 1 the late cell still catches the tail of a 60 ms first break, so a miscount was not reproduced.
findings.evidence: run_real13_all.log scenario 2 ('T11: BUSY 2 ms after its rise' ... 'T15: BUSY 78 ms'). Trace at 16904-16937 ms: leg T16 carrying T11's M at 16918, leg T17 carrying T12's at 16937. run_mc_all.log for the scale-8 figures.
findings.fix: Take the T_ARM watch off the classifier. Each cell already probes its trunk with a timer, so let the cell write the hold away if M falls before T_ARM; for a seizure with no cell, use a one-entry hold-watch beside the classifier. The classifier is then busy only for a read (~1.2 ms). Then implement rule 1 as monitor.md 4 draws it: keep 'M low at the last visit' per port (a second 64-stage delay line beside st, about 8 x '164) and give a cell only to a rise at most one pass old; older seizures are held and forwarded but not watched.
findings.realistic: Latency is real-timer measured. A wrong number from it needs a deep hop or a larger NMON plus a fast caller: likely rare, not reproduced.

findings.title: The origin takes an M rise on a held trunk as the claim even before b is dialled
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:795-804 detects the claim in o_net, which is N_NET or N_WAITCL; only `guarding` tells glare apart. A legitimate claim is made at the far end at b's ID, a relay delay after the origin's own b ID, so it can only arrive around or after the origin's f2 (net_unit.v:867-875). A rise well before b, outside the guard, is never a real claim.
findings.trigger: The (1,e) variant of stale-cell-after-unhold, or any cell that claims on a wrong count before b.
findings.consequence: The origin accepts it, drops its other directions (dmo) and connects at o_last: the wrong number goes through instead of becoming a cannot-complete.
findings.evidence: run_mc2.log [1895 ms]: 'origin=4 claimed=1' (N_NET) about 1 s before A21 dials b; origin=5 only at 2893.
findings.fix: In N_NET outside the guard, hold a rise as pending and accept it only if b arrives within a few ms (tick-phase slack between the origin's register and the far monitor, about 2 ms plus the hop); otherwise nogo. One flip-flop and a tap on tmr. It does not stop the (e+1,b) variant, which claims at b's ID.
findings.realistic: Real timing; it matters only as the second line of defence.

findings.title: NMON = 2: a third concurrent seizure is unwatched for good. A call to the exchange then fails slowly, and the whole flood is held 2 s longer
findings.mechanism: When m_free1 is empty at w_cls (net_unit.v:612), no cell is given. The hold and the forward still go ahead. Nobody here can claim.
findings.trigger: Three or more floods overlapping at one exchange within the 1.5-2.7 s a cell is held per flood (released at e's ID if e is not ours, at b's ID otherwise).
findings.consequence: The call is lost: cannot-complete 2 s after b. The unwatched trunk, every link's flood trunk and the origin's register are held that long, then released cleanly. Erlang B for cells held 1.5-2.7 s per flood: at 0.26 E, 2 cells lose 2.6% (3 cells 0.2%); 0.5 E: 7.7% (1.3%); 0.93 E (monitor.md 4's 47 exchanges): 18% (3 cells 5.4%, 5 cells 0.2%). Stale cells (stale-cell-starves-monitors) lower the effective NMON.
findings.evidence: run_mc_all.log and run_real13_all.log scenario 2: 'backward A after b: 00011', and 'T13/T14/T15 unwatched: backward A=0, still held=1'; then '2: every trunk, cell, resolver and the register released' after the far ends drop.
findings.fix: Fit NMON per monitor.md 4 (3 up to 20 exchanges, 4-5 beyond); it is a parameter already. Graceful: no stuck state, but slow.
findings.realistic: A documented limit; the consequence here is quantified and it degrades gracefully.

findings.title: One register: every claim that finds it busy with anything, even a local caller who has not dialled yet, is cannot-complete
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:282 refuses whenever r_busy (outside S_WATCH) and writes trunk -> 03 with BUSY and CLAIM (320-327). The claim handler takes claims one at a time, lowest cell first (net_unit.v:331-340, 656-676).
findings.trigger: A call to the exchange while its register serves a local dialler, its own origin call (key to b plus up to T_CLAIM), or another terminating call (h s).
findings.consequence: Refusal probability equals register occupancy: about 17% at 0.2 E, 23% at 0.3 E. Graceful and immediate at X. The far caller hears it only after dialling h s (refusal-heard-after-hs).
findings.evidence: run_mc_all.log and run_real13_all.log scenario 2: two claims in the same tick; T11 took the register and X21 rang; 'the second claim was refused: T12 claimed and listening to 03'.
findings.fix: A register pool (the maximal build). Meanwhile it is graceful.
findings.realistic: A documented limit; quantified.

findings.title: No bench covers the monitor cell of a seizure that dies young. The scale-8 benches cannot even reach the origin route of the window
findings.mechanism: tb/tb_net.v:425-438 (scenario 14) checks that the hold on a 0.9 ms blip is written away (busy_b) and that a cell was given (mb_seen > 0). It never checks that the cell is let go, or what happens if the channel is seized again. At scale 8 an origin cannot re-seize within CLR = 32 ms: key 12 + ID 16 + ~11 ms unscaled sweep.
findings.consequence: stale-cell-after-unhold passed every tree bench (all five network baselines green).
findings.evidence: work/base-*.log all PASS; work/audit/monclaim/tb_mc.v scenarios 1, 3 and 5 go red on the snapshot and green with the fix.
findings.fix: Adopt tb_mc scenarios 1, 3 and 5 (single exchange, far ends driven by the bench: cheap, about 45 s wall for all scenarios at scale 8) and tb_mc2 (end to end at real timers, about 3 min). Add a faults.py entry that removes fix (a).

findings.title: Claim-to-attach has no bound tied to the far caller's pause: `att` waits out S_WATCH, which a chattering local line can stretch to NODIG
findings.mechanism: att_refuse excludes S_WATCH (mini_marker.v:282), and att_take needs S_IDLE/TAKE/DRAIN (273-274). WATCH ends only on r_settled (SETTLE of make: 550), r_gone (CLR: 542) or r_nodig (NODIG: 542). The unit holds att with no timeout (net_unit.v:673-674). Normally the wait is at most 256 ms (a local caller who hangs up at the connect), inside the far caller's pause (at least 640 ms less ID). A local line whose makes stay under 32 ms and breaks under 256 ms holds WATCH up to NODIG (10 s). The register then attaches to the claimed trunk mid-h or mid-s: it misses pulses (pulse_rx arm semantics), so the wrong line rings or cannot-complete follows.
findings.trigger: A claim arriving just after a local connect, while that local caller's line chatters (a fault, or a hand jiggling the hook).
findings.consequence: A wrong number or cannot-complete for the far caller.
findings.evidence: Reasoning from the RTL. The normal path was measured: claim -> att -> register attached within the same ms (run_mc_all.log [1349 ms]).
findings.fix: Let the marker refuse in WATCH once WATCH has lasted a tap of its no-digit counter (say 128 ms), or have the unit withdraw att after a bound and have the marker refuse. A gate and a tap.
findings.realistic: Needs a faulty local line coinciding with a claim: rare.

findings.title: 'Claimed, cannot complete' is not heard at once: the origin connects its caller to the trunk only after h s
findings.mechanism: The refusal points the trunk at 03 (mini_marker.v:320-327), but the origin writes caller <-> trunk only at N_DONE, and N_DONE needs claimed && o_last (net_unit.v:881, 818-822). Until then the caller listens to SILENCE, written at the key (mini_marker.v:428). monitor.md 2 and common-control.md 2.3 say 'the caller hears it at once'; network.md 3's 'when the last digit is in, point the caller' matches the RTL.
findings.trigger: Any refused claim.
findings.consequence: The caller dials h s into silence and hears cannot-complete about 2 s later.
findings.evidence: RTL. tb_net scenario 8 checks the tone only after h s.
findings.fix: At the claim, also write caller -> trunk (the C path); the origin's register still counts from the caller's own M. One write. Mind the corner where the claim falls before o_last. Alternatively, correct monitor.md.
findings.realistic: Every refused call.

findings.title: The mini marker re-reads the word of every M-and-not-BUSY trunk each time it comes round
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:337-354 reads any M and not-BUSY port while idle; 358-365 returns a trunk to S_IDLE with nothing remembered (the unit has st, the marker has no equivalent). While a trunk waits to be held (a classifier backlog), or for about T_REL after a called party hangs up first under a standing far M, the marker selects it every pass. Each read holds /WS and /HW for 8 frames, pushing the unit's sweep and classifier selects to the next pass, and a line within 8 scan positions after that trunk is passed over every pass.
findings.trigger: A burst of seizures; or a terminating call where the called party hangs up first.
findings.consequence: Slower classification and sweeps; line callers delayed up to about 256 ms.
findings.evidence: Burst traces in run_mc_all.log and run_real13_all.log: mk=4 (S_READ) alternating with mk=0 while T12-T15 await their holds; cls=5 (C_WAIT) entries.
findings.fix: Give the marker a read-once bit per port (the unit's st delay line, shared on the tap).
findings.realistic: Transient and bounded.

findings.title: The release detector is an RC while the monitor's CLR is a counter. A far port released early can be re-seized before this port and its cell have let go
findings.mechanism: In the RTL both are exactly 256 ticks, so the far port's fE (port.v:183-187) and this port's fM fall within about 1 ms of each other and the cell's CLR (pulse_rx.v:93). fabric.md 3.5 makes them RC networks. With the far RC short and ours long, the far exchange can re-seize while this port still holds the old hold (BUSY, st set, so it is not re-classified or forwarded) and the old cell still counts. The gap is counted as a pulse (cnt = partial+1), then the new call's digits follow, giving the same shifted-digit claim as stale-cell-after-unhold.
findings.trigger: An abandoned flood seizure, re-seized by the far end within the RC spread.
findings.consequence: A possible wrong number; the new call is not held or forwarded here.
findings.evidence: Reasoning (RTL timers are exact).
findings.fix: Fix (b) of stale-cell-after-unhold (a cell drops on a break >= ID).
findings.realistic: Hardware tolerance only.

findings.title: A cell that claims a trunk whose resolver has already resolved re-points the trunk off the winning leg and leaves the leg and the far register up
findings.mechanism: rs_mine (net_unit.v:366) finds only busy resolvers. After w_res at R_LEG (691-708) the resolver is free. A later w_claim for the same incoming trunk writes it to 00 with CLAIM (656-658), and nothing drops the leg, which still listens to f_in.
findings.trigger: This exchange's cell still wanting (waiting on cl_st) or counting late, while a downstream exchange claims first: only with a false or duplicate claim somewhere.
findings.consequence: Two exchanges ring for one caller, and one of them hears the caller.
findings.evidence: Reasoning.
findings.fix: At w_res, free any cell whose m_port is rs_in: a comparator per cell.
findings.realistic: Needs a prior false claim.

findings.title: A link drop shorter than CLR during the flood adds a pulse at every downstream cell but not at the origin
findings.mechanism: baseband_card.v:154 and local_trunk.v:188 force A to 0 while link_up is false (about 47 us without the far clock). For a held trunk that is a break the cells count (pulse_rx.v:84-90), while the origin's register never sees it.
findings.trigger: A cable hit or clock glitch during e or b.
findings.consequence: A partial or extra count, and a possible false claim.
findings.evidence: Reasoning.
findings.fix: A cell could drop on its block's MUTE, which is not visible to the unit today, or the card could hold A through short hits.
findings.realistic: Carrier-dependent.

sound.claim: pulse_rx arming when a cell is reused cannot fabricate or double-count an edge
sound.why: probe.v publishes a sample only with port_q; net_unit.v:630-632 arms only on a sample of the new port. While disarmed, pulse_rx.v:72-77 keeps cnt, t and done at 0 and m_d = m, so at arm m_d already holds the new port's M: no edge at arm. A break in progress at arm counts only if >= HIT of it remains; a break that ended before arm is lost. Arm latency is 1-4 ms after the rise when the classifier is idle (trace: w_cls 1193 ms, armed 1194).

sound.claim: The att/att_ack handshake cannot be acked for the wrong port, acked twice, or raised before the CLAIM word is on the wire
sound.why: att_port is written only at w_claim, which needs CL_IDLE (net_unit.v:487, 669). att rises in CL_WAIT only when the whole unit queue is empty (673); ctl_queue.v:146-147 counts pushes arriving this tick. The marker's !att_ack guard (mini_marker.v:273, 282) plus att falling the tick after att_ack (674) prevent a double take. Seen in every run: CLAIM, att and the register attach all in the same ms.

sound.claim: att cannot be left high for ever, and q_empty cannot be starved
sound.why: Every marker state reaches take or refuse: S_READ with a caller candidate (r_busy=0) within ~1.2 ms; refuse skips only the single rd_done tick; S_PROBE, S_COLLECT and S_YIELD refuse at once; S_WATCH waits at most settled/CLR/NODIG (claim-attach-unbounded-in-watch). The unit's queue drains about 7500 words/s after a 156 us WAIT, and its pushes are event-driven, so nothing keeps it non-empty.

sound.claim: Two claims in one tick: one wins, one is refused cleanly
sound.why: m_want1 picks the lowest cell, and the second waits in m_want until CL_IDLE, then is refused (register busy) with CLAIM + 03. Reproduced at scale 8 and real timers (burst: X21 rings, T12 hears 03 with backward A up).

sound.claim: A claim cannot overtake a forward of the same trunk still in F_WANT/F_HUNT/F_WRITE
sound.why: The forward starts at the same w_cls as the cell and finishes within about 11-35 ms (measured 13-14 ms, 33 ms with one seizure ahead). The earliest claim, even the stale cell's (1,e) one, is at least ID plus a digit after the rise. Once a forward is in a resolver, rs_mine drops its legs in the claim tick (trace 1349 ms: res->00, T16 released).

sound.claim: Unwatched seizures and refused claims leave nothing held
sound.why: Burst runs (both scales): three unwatched trunks, one refused claim, two resolvers. All are released when the far ends drop (idle check: every port, cell, resolver, cl_st, att, forwarder, classifier and register clear).

sound.claim: The origin bank cannot have the register re-attached under it during N_WANT/N_HUNT
sound.why: The marker leaves YIELD only on r_gone, r_nodig, u_local, u_done or u_nogo. None can occur within ~20 ms of flood_go (the key's ID needs 128 ms of make), and o_gone in N_NET/N_WAITCL sees the same signals in the same tick.

sound.claim: A CLAIM or refusal written onto an already-released trunk (a no-edge hold)
sound.why: It needs m_want pending for at least T_CLAIM + T_REL, and then a 0-1 ms window between the port's rel and the cell's d_clr (both 256 ticks). If such a claim is taken, the register's gone path writes the port free (mini_marker.v S_COLLECT r_gone -> SILENCE, BSY 0). Practically unreachable.

sound.claim: The digit compare agrees with the origin
sound.why: isvc/oct in net_unit.v are the same rule as the origin's (ten pulses = 0; 8, 9, 11-15 reserved). Own-code drops and hook flashes reach the cells as breaks counted by the same HIT/CLR windows as the origin's register, so the two cannot disagree.

sound.claim: Classifier st and `mine` keep cells off the unit's own trunks and off claims coming back
sound.why: `mine` (net_unit.v:429-438) and BUSY at the sample keep outgoing trunks and legs out of cls_seen; st keeps a trunk whose BUSY fell under a standing M from being re-read as a seizure (tb_net scenario 2 is green).

notes:
Slice: monitors and claim. One wrong-number path found and reproduced; no stuck state found. Every run ended with all ports, cells, resolvers, cl_st, att, the forwarder, the classifier and the register idle.

Headline: a monitor cell given to a seizure that the classifier itself writes away (C_UNHOLD, a seizure shorter than T_ARM) is never freed. If the same channel is seized again within CLR, the stale cell counts the gap as a digit '1' (or adds 1 to e when the first break comes early) and can claim the new call for the wrong exchange.
- Reproduced at scale 8 and at real timers with bench-driven far ends: tb_mc scenario 1 at exchange 13, and scenario 5 at exchange 42 for the e+1 variant.
- Reproduced end to end between two exchanges at real timers (tb_mc2): the origin's guard abandons, and the next caller keys 1 at once. A21 dialled 1 3 2 2 1 and talked to exchange 13's line 22.
- The same stale cell also starves the 2-cell pool (scenario 3).
- A 1-package fix, in work/audit/monclaim/rtl_fix and fix.patch, closes every variant at both scales; tb_net stays green with it (88/0). The fix is: free the cell at C_UNHOLD, and drop a cell on a break >= ID.

Capacity (real timers):
- The classifier handles one trunk seizure per ~19 ms (C_HOLD = T_ARM+2 blocks it): rise-to-hold of 2/21/40/59/78 ms for 5 simultaneous seizures.
- Rise to onward leg is 14 ms idle and 33 ms with one seizure ahead (the guard budgets 12 ms a hop).
- Both resolvers filled after two forwards, so the other three were not forwarded (n_nofwd).
- The claim handler is never the bottleneck: claim -> CLAIM on the wire -> att -> register attached within 1 ms. The one register and NMON = 2 are, and both fail gracefully (immediate refusal to 03; unwatched seizure = cannot-complete after T_CLAIM). Quantified with Erlang B in the findings.

Scale: the stale-cell origin route is unreachable at scale 8 (one key 12+16 ms plus the unscaled ~11 ms sweep > CLR 32 ms), which is partly why the tree benches never met it. The origin route at real timers needed a key within ~45 ms of dial tone (6 ms margin); the transit-forwarder route is the realistic trigger.

Caveats:

- In run_fix_mc2.log the check 'A21 is not talking to X22' fails as a bench artifact: X22 lifting gets its own dial tone and so shows BUSY. The printed tx/rx lines (0/0) show A21 does not hear X22.

findings.title: A claim refused late, after its trunk port has released itself, leaves both trunk ends and an origin monitor held for good
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:282 lets a claim wait while the marker is in S_WATCH. S_WATCH (mini_marker.v:541-553) ends only on r_settled, which needs a make of at least SETTLE with no break, or on gone/nodig. So a line pulsing with makes shorter than SETTLE keeps WATCH open for as long as it pulses. While the claim waits, its far caller may hang up. The claimed port then clears itself when its fM falls (port.v:178-193, T_REL). When WATCH ends, the refusal (mini_marker.v:320-327) writes trunk<-03 with BSY and CLAIM onto that released port. It has M=0, fm=0, fe=0 (03 has no hook), so no edge is left to clear it (port.v:147, :193): it stays BUSY and CLAIM for good. At the origin, the trunk was already dropped (N_DROP, net_unit.v:823-829), and its st bit was cleared while M was low (net_unit.v:566-567). The stuck CLAIM now raises M with BUSY clear and not mine, so cls_seen (net_unit.v:283) holds the port as a fresh seizure and gives it a monitor. That M never falls, so the monitor never sees CLR. At a transit the hold would also be forwarded, and each downstream hold would keep its monitor and resolver for the same reason.
findings.trigger: A 22 and B 32 on a baseband link. B20 dials 2 1 (a local call) and then chatters (3 ms breaks, 2 ms makes) for 150 ms. A20 dials 1 3 2, timed so that B's claim lands in B's WATCH, and hangs up 2 ms after the claim. This is tb_orig S6.
findings.consequence: On the exchange: A11 and B11 are BUSY for ever and one of A's two monitor cells is held for ever. At a transit, a phantom flood holds a trunk on every link it reaches plus a monitor and a resolver at every exchange on the path, permanently. Each occurrence removes half of a default NMON=2 or NRES=2 pool. After two, the exchanges on that path can no longer claim incoming calls. The subscriber who abandoned hears nothing wrong.
findings.evidence: work/audit/origin/run_s6.log (snapshot): [393.288] B wr dst 11 src 00 bsy 1 clm 1; [393.295] B att 1 (mk 7 = WATCH); A20 hangs up, [429.289] A drops A11; B11 releases itself about 428 ms; [544.004] B mk 7->0; [544.004] att_ack REFUSED; [544.132] B wr dst 11 src 03 bsy 1 clm 1; [546.279] A mon_held 01; [546.562] A wr dst 11 src 00 bsy 1 (the phantom hold). 1.5 s later: busy A11 1 B11 1, A mon 01, and idle check FAILED. With the patched copy (rtl_fix, run_fix2.log S6), the claim is refused at att+15.7 ms ([9505.981]) while B11 can still release, and nothing is left held.
findings.fix: Take the waiting claim when WATCH ends (see watch-exit-refusal). Bound the wait so that any refusal is written while the claimed port can still release: refuse once att has waited CLR/2 (128 ms) in WATCH (rtl_fix/mini_marker.v: a 9-bit att_wait counter; one '4040 tap or half a '161). 128 ms is also early enough that a take never misses the far caller's h, which is at least ~370 ms after the claim. The general rule this breaks: never write BSY or CLAIM onto a port whose M is already low. The unit could also withdraw att itself if it sees the claimed port's M low (it has the probe).
findings.realistic: Survives real timing; the mechanism does not depend on scale. It needs the owner's WATCH to outlast T_REL (256 ms) after the far caller hangs up. That means the local caller at the owner keeps pulsing with makes under 32 ms just after being connected (a 20 pps dial dialling on, or a chattering hook or jack), while a claim lands in that WATCH and its caller abandons right after b. This is rare, but the damage is permanent and spreads along the network.

findings.title: The one register refuses incoming network calls at a rate equal to its occupancy (about 22% at 48 lines), and crossing calls refuse each other
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:282 refuses any claim at once whenever r_busy is set, outside WATCH. The register is held from a local caller's lift to its connect. It is held from an origin caller's lift to N_DONE, which comes only at o_last, the caller's last digit (net_unit.v:410, :881, :818-822), even though the claim has already fixed the path. It is also held from a claimed trunk's attach to its connect. So a claim is refused whenever the far exchange's own callers are dialling. Two floods crossing between the same pair of exchanges, each registering while the other's b arrives, are both refused (S_YIELD, mk 6), although both called lines are free.
findings.trigger: A20 dials 1 3 2 2 1 while B20 dials 1 2 2 2 1 (tb_orig S2). More generally, any claim that arrives while the far register holds a caller.
findings.consequence: Both callers dial all five digits and then hear cannot-complete. Neither called line rings. Model (work/audit/origin/model/reg1.py, reg1.out: 10 pps, 0.8 s pauses, 1-4 s reaction time, two exchanges), share of claims refused: 16 lines, 3 calls/h, 30% leaving: 7.7%. 32 lines: 14.5%. 48 lines: 21.8% (25.2% at 50% leaving, 41.5% at 5 calls/h). That is 20 to 40 times the 1% trunk blocking the network is sized for, so the register, not the trunks, is the network's bottleneck. Under overload, network completion falls towards 0 while local calls still queue. A refused origin still holds its register for the whole 1 e b h s (about 9 s), so failed attempts cost as much as successful ones. There is no livelock or stuck state; recovery is immediate when load falls.
findings.evidence: work/audit/origin/run_s2_5.log S2: [352.295] A att 1 port 12 (mk 6 reg_busy 1), A att_ack REFUSED, [352.423] A wr dst 12 src 03 bsy 1 clm 1; [370.295] B att 1 port 11 (mk 6 reg_busy 1), REFUSED, [370.423] B wr dst 11 src 03 clm 1; OBS S2: A21 ring-hi 0, B21 ring-hi 0, refusals A 1 B 1. Also tb_net scenario 8 (a local caller).
findings.fix: (1) Connect at the claim: go to N_DONE on claimed && dmo==0 and drop o_last and its one-key special case. This saves gates. It frees the origin register about 2.6 s sooner. The refused caller hears NOGO at b and not after s. It breaks the symmetry: of a crossing pair at most one fails, because the first origin's register is free before the second claim arrives. The model gives 21.8% to 19.2% at 48 lines; the gain is modest because local callers dominate occupancy. (2) A bounded claim wait of 100-300 ms, less than the far caller's pause, helps only when the register is about to free. (3) Beyond about 16 lines, a network exchange needs a register pool (the maximal build), or the monitor cell must collect h s itself. Record the figure in mini-marker.md section 8 and common-control.md section 4, which currently present the mini marker as a full pulse-flood exchange.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: it is holding-time arithmetic at real dial timing. It is systematic at busy hour, not a corner case.

findings.title: A break between the key's recognition and the seizure write is invisible to the guard, and the far monitors count the next digits as e and b
findings.mechanism: r_brk is a one-tick pulse. The origin looks at it only in N_NET and N_WAITCL (net_unit.v:862), and tmr is reset at the seizure push (net_unit.v:815). N_WANT, N_HUNT and N_SEIZE (net_unit.v:847-857, :808-817) ignore it, and the sweep takes about 10 ms plus any wait for a forwarder sweep. If e's first break begins inside that window, the trunk is seized onto a caller who is already on-hook. The far port's M then rises only at the make that ends the pulse, so every far monitor sees the rise after that pulse, which satisfies monitor rule 1. If e is a single pulse, no break follows inside the guard. The far monitors then read b as e and h as b, and the exchange whose code is (b, h) claims. The origin takes that as a genuine claim and connects at o_last.
findings.trigger: A 22, B 32. A20 dials the key with only a 20 ms make (ID is 16 ms at scale 8), so e=1's break straddles the seizure write, then dials 3 2 2 (meaning exchange 13, line 22), then one more digit, 1 (tb_orig S3b). The control (S3a) is the same number with 100 ms pauses.
findings.consequence: Exchange 32 claims a call dialled to 13. The origin connects its caller to 32's register, which reads the caller's s as h. With one more digit, B21 rings and A20 is connected to a line never dialled: a wrong number. With exactly five digits, 32's register waits for NODIG (10 s, holding 32's only register) and then gives NOGO. A class-marker exchange would complete a one-key 0 or 9 there, which is also a wrong number.
findings.evidence: work/audit/origin/run_s2_5.log S3b: [2678.999] A nst 0->1 (flood_go); [2689.283] A wr dst 11 src 20 (seizure, 10.3 ms later, during e's break); [2695.155] B cls 0->1 port 11 (the rise seen at the end of e's pulse); [3012.282] B wr dst 11 clm 1 (B claims at A's third digit); [3150.997] A N_DONE; OBS: B21 ring hi 101, A20 follows B21 4/4; FAIL x2. S3a control: nobody claims. Patched (run_fix2.log S3b): A claimed 0, B21 does not ring.
findings.fix: Add a sticky o_brk, set by r_brk in N_WANT, N_HUNT and N_SEIZE and cleared at flood_go. Abandon at h_done if it is set, without seizing, and treat it as a guard break in N_NET's first ticks (rtl_fix/net_unit.v). Cost: one flip-flop and two gates.
findings.realistic: At real timing the window is the key-to-e pause in roughly [128, 140-160] ms: ID plus the hunt, plus up to about 10 ms waiting for a forward sweep, plus queue time. e must also be a single pulse (codes 1x), or its whole train must end before the seizure. Conforming rotary dials pause much longer, so this needs a fast electronic pulse source, such as a DTR-pulsing data card or a pulse-out adaptor. The register itself accepts any pause of ID or more, so the protocol's never-a-wrong-number promise has a hole exactly there. At scale 8 the window is 8 times wider relative to dialling.

findings.title: The claimed trunk dying before N_DONE is never noticed: the caller is latched to a dead channel and later hears someone else's call on it
findings.mechanism: `claimed` is set on the first M sample (net_unit.v:795-804) and never re-examined. N_WAITCL waits only for o_last (net_unit.v:881), and N_DONE then writes caller<-trunk with BSY (net_unit.v:818-822). If the claim's M falls in between, the trunk port releases itself and becomes free for hunting, but the origin still connects the caller to it. The caller's latch then has no edge to clear it while the caller stays off-hook, because its E is 0. The next call on that channel, from this exchange's own origin or forwarder or from the far end, is heard by the stranded caller.
findings.trigger: A20 dials 1 3 2 and B claims. Link 11 is cut for 80 ms (more than T_REL and CLR at scale). A20 dials 2 1, and A connects A20<-A11. A22 then dials 1 3 2 2 0, A's sweep takes the now-free A11, B20 rings and answers (tb_orig S4). Other triggers: glare whose far origin then abandons (its own code, 8 or 9, or a hang-up), or a far reset.
findings.consequence: A20 hears nothing, and no NOGO, until it hangs up. Meanwhile it overhears B20 talking to A22, a one-way listen-in by a caller who dialled someone else (safety property 1). The far register it was claimed by has abandoned.
findings.evidence: run_s2_5.log S4: [4368.150] A CLAIMED on 11; cut; [4490.122] B wr dst 11 src 00 bsy 0 (B abandons); A still nst 5; [4786.277] A wr dst 20 src 11 bsy 1 (N_DONE onto the dead trunk); [4856.277] A wr dst 11 src 22 (A22's seizure of the same channel); OBS: A20 follows B20 4/4, FAIL. Patched (run_fix2.log S4): A abandons at the loss, A20 follows 2/4 (chance level for NOGO), ok.
findings.fix: While claimed and before N_DONE, count consecutive probe samples of `trunk` with M low. At 4, abandon with O_NOGO through N_DROP. This needs a 3-bit counter and the existing claim comparator (rtl_fix/net_unit.v `lost`). The persistence is required. A one-sample version was tried (run_fix_s6.log): when the caller's own hang-up is what dropped the claim, it fired about 1 ms before the register's gone and wrote NOGO with BSY onto the caller's already-released port, leaving A20 BUSY ([428.160] nst 5->7, [428.578] A wr dst 20 src 03 bsy 1; IDLE? busy_a bit 16). A side effect for Joel to decide on: a glare 'claim' is the far caller's dial pulses, so it breaks within about 60 ms and this fix turns documented residual glare (tb_lfull 5, 'joins two callers') into two clean cannot-completes.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing. It needs the claim's M to be lost for at least T_REL (256 ms) during the 1.5-3 s from the claim to the last digit (a link flap, far reset or glare followed by far abandon), and then a new call on that channel while the caller waits in silence. Rare, but a privacy failure and a silent dead call.

findings.title: A claim that waits out S_WATCH is refused on the tick WATCH ends, because r_busy lags r_release by a tick
findings.mechanism: att_refuse (mini_marker.v:282) excludes S_WATCH so that a claim can wait for the connect to settle, as the comment at :275-281 intends. S_WATCH ends with r_release<=1 and state<=S_IDLE (:550-553), or S_DRAIN on gone. pulse_reg's busy is a register (pulse_reg.v release_it branch), so on the next tick the marker sees state IDLE or DRAIN with r_busy still 1. att_take needs !r_busy, and att_refuse's conditions are all true, so the waiting claim is refused one tick before the register is free.
findings.trigger: B20 dials 2 1 (local). A20's b completes 1.5-3 ms after B20's s, so B's monitor claims inside B's WATCH (tb_orig S1.0 and S1.1). S1.2, where the claim arrives just after WATCH, is the control.
findings.consequence: A caller who dialled a free line (B22) hears cannot-complete; the far register was free one tick later. The outcome is clean, and there is no stuck state unless the WATCH was long (see late-refusal-no-edge-hold).
findings.evidence: work/audit/origin/run_s1.log S1.0: [391.288] B wr dst 11 src 00 clm 1; [391.295] B att 1 (mk 7 reg_busy 1); [394.004] B mk 7->0 reg_busy 1; [394.005] B att_ack REFUSED; [394.132] B wr dst 11 src 03 bsy 1 clm 1; B22 ring hi 0. S1.1 is the same at [1763.291]/[1764.001]. S1.2 control: att after WATCH, TAKEN, B22 rings. Patched (run_fix.log, run_fix2.log): S1.0 and S1.1 TAKEN, B22 rings.
findings.fix: Add && !r_release to att_refuse, one gate input; the claim is then taken at t+2 in IDLE or DRAIN. It must be combined with the bounded wait from late-refusal-no-edge-hold. An unbounded wait through a long WATCH could attach the register after the far caller's h has begun, a short count and so a wrong number; the unpatched refusal currently masks that.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: the mechanism is a one-tick lag. The window per connect is SETTLE+words, about 33 ms at real timing (8 times the 4 ms at scale). Roughly 0.1-0.3% of incoming claims at 150-400 connects an hour at the owner.

findings.title: A unit nogo that lands between the caller port's own release and the register's gone leaves the line BUSY until it is next lifted
findings.mechanism: CLR (register) equals T_REL (port) in top_net: 256 and 256, or 32 and 32 at scale. The port sees M directly (port.v:178), but pulse_reg sees it through its 1 ms probe (pulse_rx.v:93, pulse_reg.v:139), so gone rises 0-1 ms after the port has already cleared its latch. In S_YIELD a u_nogo is acted on before gone exists: the marker writes caller<-NOGO with BSY (mini_marker.v:515-523). If that word lands after the port's release, the port is BUSY with no edge to come. The unit's timers can issue that nogo independently of the hang-up: T_KEY (net_unit.v:876), T_CLAIM (:882), or 8 or 9 in the code.
findings.trigger: A caller whose flood reaches nobody hangs up about 1.74 s after b, so that the CLR moment of the hang-up coincides within about 1 ms with T_CLAIM expiry. Demonstrated in correlated form by the one-sample claim-loss fix (run_fix_s6.log, A20 left BUSY).
findings.consequence: The line is BUSY listening to 03. It is unreachable (callers hear busy) until its subscriber next lifts and hangs up, which clears it.
findings.evidence: Reasoning plus the correlated reproduction in work/audit/origin/run_fix_s6.log: [428.160] A nst 5->7 before r_gone at 429, [428.578] A wr dst 20 src 03 bsy 1, and at the end IDLE? busy_a 0000000000010000 (A20).
findings.fix: Make the register's gone lead the port's release: CLR a few ms shorter than T_REL (the register's taps are separate from the port RC). Alternatively, in S_YIELD's nogo branch, write BSY only while the register's `hook` reads off-hook. That is one gate, but it changes what a caller in mid-break hears after a guard abandon (tb_net 7).
findings.realistic: About 1 in 1000 of calls that time out while their caller is hanging up. The effect is temporary, until the next off-hook.

findings.title: A claim arriving on an origin trunk after dmo or N_DROP has let it go is classified as a fresh incoming seizure
findings.mechanism: dmo (net_unit.v:800, :831-837) and N_DROP (:823-829) write the dropped trunk free and remove it from d_held, so `mine` no longer covers it. st[port] is set only if M was seen while the port was BUSY (:566-570). A second copy's claim, from a ring's long way or a claim that crosses the T_CLAIM drop, that lands after the drop therefore meets M up, BUSY clear, not mine and st clear. cls_seen (:283) holds it listening to 00, gives it a monitor, and forwards it if the link is not strapped.
findings.trigger: A ring or mesh where the same owner hears the flood on two paths whose A delays differ by more than about 1.5 ms (MF8 at 0.5 ms a hop: 3 or more extra hops), or a claim reaching the origin just after its 2 s T_CLAIM.
findings.consequence: A phantom seizure: the trunk plus a monitor are held, and at a transit a steady-M flood runs onward, until the owner's refused copy releases about T_REL to 2xT_REL later. No wrong number, because the phantom's M never pulses; it wastes trunks and monitors at busy hour.
findings.evidence: tb_orig S5, with two direct links A-B (E and jumpered N), 3 phases (run_s2_5.log S5.0-S5.2): the second CLAIM ([6738.563]) reaches A before A's drop ([6739.428]), so st is set and there is no phantom. The race is therefore lost only when the second path is slower, which is the ring case this design documents in network.md 3.3.
findings.fix: Keep a dropped origin trunk masked from the classifier (as `mine`) until its M has been seen low and then for T_REL, or have the owner not raise CLAIM on a trunk whose forward M has fallen. The cost is about one counter per direction on the unit.
findings.realistic: Only in rings or meshes with unequal path delay, and at the T_CLAIM boundary. Low frequency and temporary.

findings.title: A claim is accepted on a single 1 ms sample of M on any held trunk
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:795-804 accepts the first sp_m sample on any d_held trunk as the claim. It drops every other direction at once (dmo) and at o_last connects the caller to that trunk.
findings.trigger: A single false A=1 sample on any held trunk during the 2-4 s flood, from a carrier whose A can glitch (MF8 S-bit errors, a radio link).
findings.consequence: The true owner's direction is dropped, and the caller is connected into a far hold listening to 00. It hears silence, not NOGO, until it hangs up. Not a wrong number unless the owner sat behind the kept trunk.
findings.evidence: Reasoning. channel-cards.md 5 measures 0 spurious A transitions on MF8 at 1e-1, so the risk depends on the carrier.
findings.fix: Require the claim M to stand for 2-4 samples. This shares the `lost` counter of claimed-trunk-loss-listen-in.
findings.realistic: Not on baseband or local trunks. Possible on carriers not yet designed.

findings.title: The mini marker re-reads a trunk port showing M with BUSY clear every other pass, and cannot see the eight ports after it meanwhile
findings.mechanism: S_IDLE (mini_marker.v:337-345) sends any fresh M.!BUSY port to S_READ, and a trunk's word sends it straight back to S_IDLE (:365). The marker keeps no per-port 'already read' bit like the unit's st. The read waits a pass for its select, then collects for 8 frames. The marker is therefore in S_READ at the turns of ports T+1..T+8 in every pass, and never sees a caller there. Each select also blocks the unit's /WS reads for 8 frames, costing its sweep about one pass per collision.
findings.trigger: Any trunk with M up and BUSY down. Normally this lasts at most about 2xT_REL: after a claimed trunk is dropped, or when the called party hangs up first (tb_net 2). It would last for ever if such a state were ever permanent.
findings.consequence: Lines numbered T+1 to T+8 get no dial tone while it lasts, typically up to about 0.5 s real. The unit's sweeps stretch by about 30-50% during it.
findings.evidence: Reasoning from the code. It was not triggered while the marker was idle in these runs: in S5 the marker was in YIELD throughout.
findings.fix: Add a per-port 'word said trunk, M has stood since' bit in the marker, like st in net_unit.v:277, or skip a port whose last read was a trunk until its M is seen low. About one package (a 64-stage delay line).
findings.realistic: Frequent but short: every call whose called party hangs up first.

findings.title: No network bench exercises the origin and marker races found here
findings.mechanism: tb_net, tb_chain, tb_lnet, tb_lfull and tb_lchain never place a claim inside S_WATCH, never run two floods crossing in opposite directions, never break between the key and the seizure, never lose a claimed trunk before N_DONE, and never delay a refusal past the claimed port's release.
findings.trigger: Not applicable (a coverage gap, not a runtime scenario).
findings.consequence: Five of the defects above pass the committed sequence.
findings.evidence: work/audit/origin/tb_orig.v scenarios S1-S6 are red on the snapshot (run_s1.log, run_s2_5.log, run_s6.log) and green with the three fixes except S2, which is the register limit (run_fix2.log: 19 checks, 0 errors).

sound.claim: flood_go is never raised while the origin bank is busy, so it is never lost
sound.why: The marker leaves S_YIELD on its own only on r_gone or r_nodig, which are o_gone to the unit (net_unit.v:413). o_gone is checked every tick in N_WANT, N_NET and N_WAITCL. In N_HUNT, N_SEIZE and N_DONE the unit is blind for at most one sweep (about 10-20 ms). r_gone cannot occur until CLR (256 ms real, 32 ms at scale) after the key's digit ended, and a new flood_go needs a new attach plus a whole digit. So a stale origin cannot meet a new caller. The margin is 1.6x or more at scale 8 and over 10x at real timing.

sound.claim: restart, local_go, done and nogo reach the marker in S_YIELD
sound.why: att_refuse excludes the ticks on which they arrive (mini_marker.v:320-321). att_take cannot occur in S_YIELD because r_busy is set. y_nogo holds nogo across ticks with no queue room (:515-517). The unit decides O_LOCAL or O_NOGO only while !o_gone, and reaches N_END within a few ticks. A lost `done` (only possible if the caller has left) is benign: the far release clears the caller's latch through fE.

sound.claim: The own-code restart cannot erase or split the caller's h
sound.why: restart lands 2-3 ticks after N_END, about ID after b's digit, so the caller's h cannot complete in that window. pulse_reg's restart clears ndig and digits but not pulse_rx's cnt (pulse_reg.v restart branch), so a partly counted h survives. hold=3 (mini_marker.v:509) covers the two-register path of u_restart.

sound.claim: The att/att_ack handshake cannot double-take or be lost
sound.why: att is a level held until the one-tick att_ack. The marker masks a re-take with !att_ack. w_claim is serialised by cl_st (net_unit.v:487, :672-676). att is raised only once the unit's queue is empty (CL_WAIT q_empty), so a refusal always follows the CLAIM word. The one flaw is the tick after a release (watch-exit-refusal).

sound.claim: The classifier never holds the origin's own trunk as an incoming seizure
sound.why: The confirm pass visits each candidate exactly once, and its next visit comes after h_done. From that point `mine` covers o_cand in N_SEIZE and then d_held (net_unit.v:432-433). A far seizure seen at or before the confirm visit clears h_ok instead (:779-785).

sound.claim: The origin's hunt cannot take a trunk the forwarder is about to write, or the reverse
sound.why: The forwarder's F_WRITE cannot stall: a resolver free at classification stays free, because only F_WRITE allocates resolvers, so its words land within about 1 ms. The next sweep's confirm pass is at least 9 ms later and sees BUSY. The same holds for the origin's N_SEIZE write against a following forward sweep.

sound.claim: Every origin exit leaves no trunk held
sound.why: Every exit from N_NET and N_WAITCL (hang-up, nodig, guard, 8 or 9, own code, T_KEY, T_CLAIM) goes through N_DROP, which drops every d_held trunk (net_unit.v:823-829). A caller who leaves during N_HUNT gets no seizure. During N_SEIZE the seizure is written onto an on-hook caller (forward A=0, so the far end sees nothing) and dropped on the next tick. tb_net 3-7 and 11, and tb_orig S3a, end idle.

sound.claim: A claim and o_gone, or a claim and the dmo drop, on the same tick are consistent
sound.why: N_DROP pushes d_held, including trunks not yet dropped by dmo, and clears dmo. The default w_orig branch drops only dmo. N_DONE requires dmo==0, so the others' drops are always pushed first (net_unit.v:806-839, :881).

sound.claim: A genuine claim arriving before the origin's own b is recognised is handled
sound.why: The far exchange's tick phase can lead by up to 1 ms. claimed is then set in N_NET, and it is not counted as glare because tmr is far past the guard. f2 follows at b, and N_WAITCL connects at o_last.

sound.claim: The far hold's backward A is 0 until a claim, including through one-leg transit patches
sound.why: Holds listen to port 00, which is never fitted, so E=0. A one-leg patch carries the next hop's backward A, which is recursively 0 until that hop claims. Only a claim or glare on some downstream link raises it. Downstream glare returns inside the origin's guard for about 10 hops and is counted: the documented residual glare.

sound.claim: Duplicate claims over two direct links do not create a phantom
sound.why: In tb_orig S5, at three phases, the owner's second CLAIM reached the origin about 0.3 ms after the first and about 1 ms before the origin's dmo drop. The origin therefore saw M under BUSY, st was set, and the dropped copy was left alone. The call completed (B21 rang), and the second copy was refused and released cleanly.

sound.claim: The guard is not measurably weakened by queue delay after the seizure push

After the push, the word and the caller's-turn capture add at most about 3 ms: about 2% of the real 128 ms guard (about 20% of the scaled 16 ms).

sound.why: T_KEY (5 s) and T_CLAIM (2 s after b) both expire before the register's NODIG (10 s from the last digit), so the unit decides first. The mini marker's key test takes a count of 1 only (mini_marker.v:414). keyed and ctx_clm stop a second flood from an own-code call or from a claimed trunk (tb_net 15).

sound.claim: Glare is rare
